findings.proposition: Cheaper assigned prices increase stated subscription interest, with a much lower full-intent profile at the high end; this is not revealed demand.
findings.qualification: Do not rename reported likelihood a purchase probability, demand curve or actual price elasticity.

findings.proposition: The cheapest price is not the strongest price-times-interest candidate. Gross and assumed-cost contribution proxies favour different closely competing mid-price candidates in the intended first-candidate design.
findings.qualification: Retain any failure to realise the anticipated different point leaders; do not manufacture or silently rewrite it. These indices do not measure revenue or profit.

findings.proposition: Close mid-price proxy leads are uncertain and sensitive to the predeclared variable-cost scenarios, so recommend further behavioural validation rather than a certain optimal price.
findings.qualification: Not equivalence from a wide CI, no data-chosen cost scenario, no universally optimal point leader.

findings.proposition: Price-related incomplete observation makes valid-case interest conditional; show conservative all-assigned sensitivity, missing-data ranges and fixed-weight denominators before generalising.
findings.qualification: q_0 is a lower coding sensitivity for recorded positive intent, not observed rejection or a bound on sales. Baseline weights do not fix missingness.

findings.proposition: The prespecified time-pressed-family audience has higher stated interest at the same mid-price assignments, without establishing that children/time pressure causes that interest.
findings.qualification: Do not turn an observational audience contrast into attribute causality or a proven subgroup price optimum.

findings.proposition: Value, affordability and intent show correlated diagnostic patterns; these support interpretation but not independently identified causal mechanisms.
findings.qualification: Price randomisation does not randomise perceived value, trust or affordability separately.

findings.proposition: Hypothetical use and certainty are selectively routed follow-ups, not independent evidence of actual uptake or all-household usage.
findings.qualification: Never generalise P10's frequency to all assigned households or treat hypothetical days as measured behaviour.

findings.proposition: An apparent largest proxy point estimate is not a certain economically optimal price.
findings.qualification: Preserve candidate uncertainty and all fixed cost scenarios.

findings.proposition: Older comfortable households already paying for planning can look unusually interested but their price-specific cells are too small for rates or targeting claims.
findings.qualification: Suppress each n<40 component rate/proxy/contrast. Do not rescue it with a pooled n across unlike prices.

findings.proposition: Stated intent and assumed-cost arithmetic establish neither actual demand nor sales, elasticity, uptake, profit, ROI or an effect on all UK households.
findings.qualification: Label the estimands and scenario assumptions; preserve randomisation and missingness limits.
